1.why: auth() rejects any session whose userId does not match the account and suppliedIdentifier() returns 403 for any client-supplied user identifiers, so MFA endpoints only ever operate on the session owner's settings.

2.why: The OTP is checked only against the pending secret of the single session-bound account in /api/mfa/verify, so there is no path by which the same code would work for any other user.

3.why: /api/mfa/verify sets account.enabled=true without deleting or rotating any sessions (sessions are removed only on login, logout, or timeout), so previous sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM-encrypted via encrypt(secret) and recovery codes are stored as a SHA-256 hash plus AES-GCM ciphertext, never in plain text.

5.why: token(), base32(), recoveryCode(), and the AES key all derive randomness exclusively from crypto.getRandomValues, a CSPRNG.

6.why: The session token is only in an HttpOnly;Secure;SameSite=Strict cookie, the CSRF token is held in a JS variable, and no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie is used anywhere.

7.why: The server validates email (emailOK), phone (phoneOK), OTP (/^\d{6}$/), and recovery code format, enforces JSON content-type and a 4KB body cap, and uses no SQL at all.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered through esc() (textContent-based escaping) and a per-response nonce CSP blocks any injected inline script or style.

9.why: The server issues no redirects and the client router navigates only to a fixed allow-list of hash routes, so no open or user-controlled redirect exists.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on every response.

11.why: The bank_session cookie is set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes (and cleared with the same attributes on logout).

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces and no secrets in URLs, but the client log() function writes the OTP secret, test OTP, and recovery codes into the on-page log panel and console.log, so secrets are not kept out of logs.

13.why: Pending verifications carry a 5-minute expiry and are marked used after one success, and recovery codes are marked used upon redemption, making codes single-use and time-bound.

14.why: Five failed OTP attempts set p.locked for 10 minutes and five failed recovery attempts set account.recoveryLocked for 10 minutes.

15.why: Login deletes the old session and issues a fresh random token, auth() enforces 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
